title: A profile's allowed_tools and disallowed_tools are a boundary only on claude-p; the tmux drivers never pass them
problem: profileWire has no disallowed_tools field, so every profile's deny list is dropped on unmarshal; allowed_tools reaches only the headless claude-p driver (--allowedTools). Every tmux driver launches without either, and the host-side PreToolUse hooks gate only ship, phase, role (Edit|Write path-scoped) and docdelete. A helper profile that lists curl, wget, WebFetch or git commit as disallowed therefore has no such boundary when it runs on claude-tmux or codex-tmux, its default. Found by the ADR-0106 security review of the recovery agent's profile (2026-09-26); the same holds for failure-advisor and failure-adjudicator.
fix: Either project allowed_tools and disallowed_tools into the tmux launches (the claude CLI accepts --allowedTools and --disallowedTools interactively) and parse disallowed_tools in profileWire, or state in every profile that the sandbox (write grants, read_only_repo, allow_network) is the boundary and drop the inert lists. Until then every helper profile that runs without network need should set sandbox.allow_network false (deliverable-recovery does).
acceptance: A profile that disallows Bash(curl:*) cannot run curl on claude-tmux, or the lists are gone from every profile and the docs say the sandbox is the boundary.
profileWire either parses disallowed_tools or the field is rejected as unknown.
A wiring test proves the projection for every tmux driver.
